claims.text: Active Learning Bayesian Optimization will identify RHEA compositions with significantly improved combinations of strength, ductility, and low weight relative to compositions developed using conventional thermo-kinetic analyses and simulations.
The relevant RHEA design space is a broad compositional space containing multiple principal elements.
The initial candidate space has no optimized processing history.
Active Learning Bayesian Optimization can iteratively refine candidate compositions using small batches of targeted high-fidelity experimental data.
The proposed design is confined to elemental concentration ranges of 5–35% per element.
The proposed dwell-time range is 10–60 minutes.
Elemental distribution and resulting microstructural phase formation mediate the balance among intrinsic strength, ductility, and density.
Iterative updating with experimental feedback allows Bayesian optimization to narrow the RHEA design space efficiently.
The optimization will direct the search toward compositional regions whose microstructures provide a favorable combination of mechanical properties and low weight.
The selected RHEA compositions will have measurably improved strength and ductility relative to traditionally designed alloys.
The selected RHEA compositions will have reduced weight relative to traditionally designed alloys.
Traditional thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation methods do not efficiently explore the full RHEA compositional space.
The effectiveness of the optimization may be limited to the specified elemental ranges, temperatures, and dwell times.
Performance within the specified domain may not translate to compositions or processing conditions outside that domain.
Variation in experimental conditions and initial data quality can affect the magnitude of improvements produced by the framework.
